Quantum Error Correction Thresholds

This paper surveys the surface code and its role in fault-tolerant quantum
computing. Quantum error correction is essential because physical qubits are
noisy and decohere quickly.

The surface code achieves a high error-correction threshold by using local
stabilizer measurements on a two-dimensional lattice of data and ancilla
qubits. Errors are detected by measuring parity checks known as stabilizers.

Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires error rates below a threshold.
Below this threshold, increasing the code distance exponentially suppresses
logical errors. The threshold for the surface code is approximately one
percent under standard circuit-level noise models.

Topological error correction is attractive because stabilizer measurements
are local and require only nearest-neighbor interactions.
